Example dataset: murine splenic B cells

Source: R/data.R
tevra_example.Rd

A subset of the 10x Genomics murine splenocyte dataset with paired gene expression and BCR sequencing, used in the TEVRA tutorial.

Usage

tevra_example

Format

A SingleCellExperiment with 2,000 highly variable genes and 3,430 cells:

assays

logcounts: log-normalised expression

reducedDims

PCA, UMAP

colData

Per-cell metadata with 19 columns:

orig.ident

Tissue of origin (spleen)

nCount_RNA

Total UMI counts per cell

nFeature_RNA

Number of genes detected per cell

percent.mt

Percentage of counts from mitochondrial genes

celltype

Broad cell type annotation (B cell)

S.Score, G2M.Score

Cell cycle phase scores from Seurat's CellCycleScoring()

Phase

Assigned cell cycle phase (G1, S or G2M)

Bcelltype

B cell subset annotation

CTgene_BCR

V(D)J and constant gene usage of the heavy and light chains

CTnt_BCR

CDR3 nucleotide sequences of the heavy and light chains

CTaa_BCR

CDR3 amino acid sequences of the heavy and light chains

CTstrict_BCR

Strict clonotype identifier from scRepertoire, used as the default clone definition

clonalProportion_BCR

Proportion of cells in the sample belonging to the cell's clone

clonalFrequency_BCR

Number of cells in the sample belonging to the cell's clone

cloneSize_BCR

Binned clonal expansion category

CTaa_BCR_IGH

Heavy chain CDR3 amino acid sequence

CTaa_BCR_IGL

Light chain CDR3 amino acid sequence

metadata

List of additional objects:

graphs

Cell-cell graphs computed on the full gene set with Seurat's FindNeighbors():

RNA_snn

Shared nearest neighbour graph

Source

Dataset from 10x Genomics (https://www.10xgenomics.com/datasets/integrated-gex-and-vdj-analysis-of-connect-generated-library-from-mouse-splenocytes-2-standard-6-0-1), licensed under CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Modified from the original: cell types were assigned with Seurat, clonal identity was computed with scRepertoire, and the object was converted to a SingleCellExperiment and restricted to the top 2,000 highly variable genes.
